subject.title: improve: warn before non-ClawHub plugin installs

question: Should OpenClaw make all non-ClawHub plugin installs fail closed without interactive confirmation or `--acknowledge-non-clawhub-install`, and should this policy land only after the ClawHub trust-metadata rollout?
rationale: The implementation is mechanically coherent, but it deliberately changes established CLI and automation behavior and coordinates with an external trust rollout; source inspection cannot authorize that product and compatibility policy.

options.title: Accept After Trust Rollout
options.body: Approve the fail-closed policy, confirm the ClawHub dependency is ready, refresh the branch against main, and land the exact reviewed head.

options.title: Preserve Default Compatibility
options.body: Keep existing noninteractive behavior by default and expose stronger acknowledgement through an explicit opt-in strict policy.

options.title: Pause For Joint Design
options.body: Hold the PR until the OpenClaw and ClawHub trust contracts and rollout order are approved together.

recommendation.title: Accept After Trust Rollout
recommendation.body: Approve the fail-closed policy, confirm the ClawHub dependency is ready, refresh the branch against main, and land the exact reviewed head.

likelyOwner.reason: The canonical install boundary and adjacent fail-closed security policy trace most strongly to their current-main history, making them the best available owner for the compatibility decision.
